evidence_fragments.content: Synthesizing 364 sources, we formalize the “Silicon Shield” three-layer architecture: Data Pipes, Model Pipelines, and Decision Interfaces.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/093_2026_Integrating mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence to combat emerging viral syndemics A systematic review.pdf
evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase (visual p.5)] PRISMA 2020 flow diagram: 114,445 database records identified (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Jan 1990 - Jul 2026); 80,170 removed before screening; 34,268 screened; 30,432 excluded; 3,836 full-text assessed; 3,475 excluded; 3 organizational/outbreak news reports added; 364 total sources included.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/093_2026_Integrating mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence to combat emerging viral syndemics A systematic review.pdf

locator.section_or_table: Section 2.3 Selection process and PRISMA flow framework

evidence_fragments.content: Despite the relevance of these individual metrics, the extreme methodological heterogeneity across computational domains, encompassing fundamentally different model classes (mechanistic ODEs, agent-based simulations, convolutional neural networks, gradient boosting, large language models), distinct data modalities (genomic sequences, medical images, time-series surveillance data, environmental variables), and incompatible outcome definitions, precluded a pooled quantitative meta-analysis using any single metric [83,84]. This challenge is well recognised in systematic reviews of AI applications in healthcare, where substantial heterogeneity (I2>98%) frequently persists even within relatively homogeneous subgroups [75,85]. Accordingly, results were synthesised using a structured narrative approach following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) reporting guideline

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/093_2026_Integrating mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence to combat emerging viral syndemics A systematic review.pdf
evidence_fragments.content: Notably, the evidence base remains dominated by COVID-19, is largely evaluated using point-error metrics (MAE, MAPE, RMSE) rather than proper probabilistic scoring rules or formal decision-utility criteria

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/093_2026_Integrating mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence to combat emerging viral syndemics A systematic review.pdf
evidence_fragments.content: The CONSORT-AI and SPIRIT-AI extensions provide the first international standards for clinical trials of AI systems, mandating clear descriptions of human-AI interaction, algorithm inputs/outputs, and error analyses

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/093_2026_Integrating mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence to combat emerging viral syndemics A systematic review.pdf
evidence_fragments.content: to transition the “Silicon Shield” from a theoretical framework into an operational global defence system against emerging viruses and associated syndemic crisis, we propose a “Modular Reference Architecture” structured across three functional tiers

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/093_2026_Integrating mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence to combat emerging viral syndemics A systematic review.pdf
evidence_fragments.content: Together, these DAG-guided, doubly robust, and simulation-based causal inference strategies would enable the “Silicon Shield” to move beyond correlational surveillance toward actionable, equity-informed causal intelligence for pandemic response.

Availability of data and materials
Data sharing does not apply to this article as no novel data was generated during the current study.

capability_assessments.rationale: Systematic review of 364 sources proposing a conceptual 3-layer 'Silicon Shield' reference architecture without implementing or evaluating a persistent-state learned/hybrid transition model.

limitations: Systematic review only; no original model implementation, dataset, or empirical evaluation.
